_README: EXAMPLE policy for the cross-provider egress guard. Copy this to ~/.claude/mcp-gate-policy.json and EDIT the allow-lists for YOUR environment. The default is DENY for any network/send-class tool whose destination is not explicitly allow-listed below — so an empty or trimmed list fails closed (safe), never open. Contains hostnames and tool-name globs ONLY: no secrets, no tokens. Both Claude Code (mcp-guard.sh / bash-egress-guard.sh) and Codex (codex-egress.patch) read this same file and fail closed if it is missing, unreadable, or invalid JSON. See docs/THREAT-MODEL.md for the enforcement model and docs/INSTALL.md to deploy.
_require_token_comment: OPTIONAL: tool-name globs that require a fresh single-use confirmation token before they run (a second factor for destructive/high-risk tools). Independent of egress. Leave empty if you do not use a token-gate hook.

egress._non_egress_servers_comment: Checked FIRST. Local / loopback / filesystem MCP servers that never make agent-driven egress to arbitrary hosts — they skip the gate entirely. Replace these with YOUR local-only servers. If any of these is ever swapped for a hosted backend, REMOVE it from this list.
egress._url_tools_comment: Mode 1 — tools that carry an explicit URL in tool_input. Allowed iff EVERY extracted host is in allow_hosts. A URL tool with no extractable host is denied (destination unverifiable). Deceptive hosts (userinfo-spoof, trailing-dot, punycode, IP-literal) are normalized to their true host before matching.
egress._allow_hosts_comment: EXAMPLE host allow-list — REPLACE with the hosts YOUR agents legitimately need. Pin specific subdomains; avoid multi-tenant wildcards (e.g. *.somecloud.app) that an attacker can also provision a tenant on. Vendor-owned trust anchors (e.g. *.anthropic.com) are acceptable wildcards.
egress._connector_tools_comment: Mode 2 — fixed-backend connectors that carry NO URL in tool_input (the destination is the connector backend, implicit in the tool name). Allowed iff the full tool name matches an allow_connectors glob; an unknown or renamed connector is denied.
egress._connector_owner_scope_comment: OPTIONAL finer scope on a connector class: a connector matching the glob may act only on allow-listed resource owners (read from owner/org/organization/repoOwner fields, owner/repo in repository/full_name, and github.com/<owner> URLs). A positively-identified disallowed owner is denied; a call with no detectable owner passes. Example below scopes any github connector to a single owner — replace 'your-org' with yours, or delete this key to allow any owner.
egress._network_name_globs_comment: Mode 3 — fail-closed catch-all. Any tool whose NAME signals network/send behavior but matches neither Mode 1 nor Mode 2 is denied unless its server is in non_egress_servers. This is the backstop for HTTP/send-class tools from arbitrary MCP servers.
egress._github_shell_comment: OPTIONAL (shell hooks only): owner/host allow-lists for git/gh WRITE operations run via the shell (git push, gh pr create, gh api POST, ...). Reads (clone/fetch/pull, gh view/list) are never gated. Armed only when present — delete these keys to disable. Owner-scope denies a write to a disallowed GitHub owner; host allow-list denies a write to a deceptive/non-GitHub host.
